clue.text: Frustrate pair going round mouth of river for starter

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to frustrate or thwart it

indicators.note: the word for pair encircles the next piece, wrapping round it

parts.note: both means the pair of them

indicators.note: the mouth of the word river is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone thwarts a couple heading round an estuary, apparently as an opening move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts R, the opening letter of 'river' signalled by 'mouth of', inside BOTH. 'for' is a link; 'starter' is a soup served as the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish barley-and-mutton soup is commonly served as the first course of a meal.

clue.text: Game's not finished before Frenchman's sandwich

indicators.note: the game's name lacks its ending, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and hoops
Monsieur is the French title for a man

explanation.surface: An unfinished game comes before a Frenchman's lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' drops the game's final letter. 'Game's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is only for the surface and supplies no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A croque-monsieur is a toasted ham-and-cheese sandwich from French cafés.

definitions.meaning: in informal British use, a ... sum or ... result is a decent, fairly large one
a ... is a container for odds and ends, such as a sink ... or desk ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an informal adjective for reasonably large or decent and a noun for a small holder of oddments.

clue.text: The lady's said in Calais to include note before end of May about genetics

indicators.note: the first pieces take in the note, which sits within them

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman, the lady's
dit is French for said, Calais being a French port
E is a musical note in the scale

indicators.note: the end of the word May is its final letter

explanation.surface: A convoluted remark about a woman speaking French in Calais and a musical note before the end of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts E inside HERDIT, giving HEREDIT; 'end of' takes Y from May. 'before' and 'about' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Heredity is the passing of traits from parents to offspring, the subject studied by genetics.

indicators.note: the word is placed inside the word for water

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit is sitting in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a kind of fruit.

indicators.note: spotted means seen within the words, the answer being found inside the run forest Reynard

explanation.surface: In the forest, a fox was seen by three people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' signals the letters lie inside 'forest Reynard'; Reynard is the traditional name of the fox in fables.
explanation.definitionFit: A trey is the three in a suit of cards or on dice.

parts.note: a brae is a Scots word for a hillside or steep slope, so read cryptically it is a slope found north of the border, also the name of a Scottish bank

explanation.walkthrough: A brae is a Scottish hillside: literally a 'bank' of Scotland, and also the name of a famous Scottish bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A brae is a hillside or riverbank in Scots usage, literally a slope belonging to that country.

clue.text: You and I back majority that are farthest to the left

parts.note: you and I together are we
the stern is the back of a ship
the majority is most of something

explanation.surface: You and I support the majority who sit furthest to the left politically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that are' is a link. On a conventional map west is on the left, so the far left is the far west.
explanation.definitionFit: On a map with north at the top, the point lying farthest to the left is the one most to the west.

definitions.meaning: read literally, a case argued over a border line
something uncertain whose outcome could go either way

explanation.definitionFit: A matter only just on one side of a dividing line is uncertain, and literally a case about a boundary.

clue.text: Security Don arranged out of town

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters of Security Don are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A university don has arranged security somewhere out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles the eleven letters of SECURITY DON.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural land lying away from towns and cities is what lies out of town.

clue.text: Egg on very useful members initially

indicators.note: initially signals taking the opening letter of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: Someone encourages very useful members of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' reads as 'urge', but 'Egg' alone is the definition and 'on' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovum is the female reproductive cell, an egg in biological terms.

parts.note: an ad is a notice advertising something

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: Mick is a short form of Michael, so Michael's is Mick's

explanation.surface: A notice says what Michael's blend is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns MICKS, the familiar form of 'Michael's', into its sound-alike MIX.
explanation.definitionFit: To admix is to mingle or blend one substance with another.

clue.text: Take off first red garment in sketch

indicators.note: take off means remove one letter from the garment's name

parts.note: a skirt is a garment

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word red

explanation.surface: Someone is told to remove a red garment first in a sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like the definition (a skit is a take-off), but it is the removal signal; 'first' takes R from 'red'. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch, often a parody.

definitions.meaning: growers join a shoot of one plant onto another to propagate fruit trees

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for toil and the horticultural verb for joining a scion to rootstock.

indicators.note: the drink loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: squash is a fruit cordial drink

explanation.surface: A soft drink loses its froth on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing its head' removes the S that begins SQUASH; squash is a diluted fruit cordial in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To quash is to suppress or crush, as a rebellion.

parts.note: figurative is read as relating to figures, so this means competent with numbers

explanation.walkthrough: 'figurative' usually means metaphorical; here it means to do with figures, numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being competent with numbers is the arithmetic counterpart of being able to read.

clue.text: Old fool found at the end of the line

definitions.meaning: a foolish elderly man in British slang

definitions.text: found at the end of the line
definitions.meaning: railway ... stand at the end of a track

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a doddery old man in slang and a shock-absorbing stop at the end of a railway track.

parts.note: the bay tree is a laurel
to watch is to see or look at

explanation.surface: Stan Laurel goes to see a programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel' suggests the comedian; it is the bay tree. The programme is the American lifeguard TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a long-running television series about lifeguards.

indicators.note: exercising suggests the letters of for fun being put through their paces and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is working out for fun in a deciding match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercising' rearranges FOR FUN; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-off is an extra race or vote held to decide a tie.

indicators.note: cooked signals that the letters of the word are reworked

parts.note: cum is Latin for with, as in combined with

explanation.surface: Aspic is cooked together with pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges ASPIC into CAPSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicum is the genus of sweet and chilli peppers.

indicators.note: the street is out, on the outside, with the other word placed within

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to pine is to long for something

explanation.surface: A musical instrument has been sent a long way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' places ST outside PINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord-type keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Point in bridge in which to deposit eggs

indicators.note: the compass letter goes inside the word for bridge

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one
W is the compass point west

explanation.surface: A point on a bridge where fish might lay their eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point; 'in which to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and frogs spawn by depositing masses of eggs in water.

clue.text: In full it's denoting inflammatory disease

definitions.meaning: the contraction it's written out in full as two words
the suffix used in medicine for inflammation, as in tonsillitis

explanation.definitionFit: The suffix marks inflammation in medical terms, and the same letters are the expanded form of a contraction.

parts.note: S to W spans five letters of the alphabet, S, T, U, V and W, written out as the range
the word linking the first and last letters of that five-letter range
the closing letter of the five-letter range running from S

explanation.surface: A packing instruction with five letters on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The five letters S, T, U, V, W run from S to W, which is how the range is written out.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack goods away neatly, as cargo in a hold.

clue.text: Cheek of jay taking another bird

parts.note: jay is the spelt-out name of the letter J
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: The cheek of a jay picking on another bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jay' looks like the bird, but it is the name of the letter J; 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A jowl is the lower part of the cheek or jaw.

parts.note: a disciple of Jesus who was not certain, refusing to believe in the resurrection without seeing for himself

explanation.walkthrough: The follower is one of the twelve apostles, who doubted until he saw the wounds (John 20:25).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a sceptic, after the apostle who would not believe without proof.

indicators.note: off signals that the letters of the following words are disordered

parts.note: the letters of cable's including the final s

explanation.surface: Something cuts the width off a cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CABLES WIDTH, the s of 'cable's' counting as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchblade is a flick knife, something that cuts.
